value_note: Scores are relative ranks within the comparison area, not calibrated experience scores. N/A = not measurable, never 0. On crossings, park paths, bridges and streets with a missing record, a score rests on fewer indicators than listed, because the others were not measured there (share of routable length: Quiet & Relax 30%, Spatial Comfort 31%).
score_method: Each scored indicator → percentile rank 0–100 among segments of the comparison area that have a value (ties take the lowest rank; "lower is better" indicators reversed as 100 − rank). Dimension score = equal-weight mean of the indicator percentiles available on that segment. N/A when none is available; missing values are never 0. Validation/context indicators never enter a score.

source_labels.trees: NYC Parks Forestry Tree Points (structure = Full)
source_labels.tnc_landcover: NYC Land Cover 2021 (6 in) — TNC / UVM Spatial Analysis Lab
source_labels.nypd_complaints: NYPD Complaint Data Historic (qgea-i56i) + Current YTD (5uac-w243)
source_labels.dohmh_no2: NYC DOHMH Air Quality (NYCCAS annual NO₂)
source_labels.subway: MTA Subway Entrances and Exits: 2024 (entry allowed)
source_labels.seating+osm_walk: NYC DOT Seating Locations · OpenStreetMap pedestrian network (OSMnx walk graph)
source_labels.ramps+lion: NYC DOT Pedestrian Ramp Locations · NYC Street Centerline (LION) — NYC DCP
source_labels.waterfront_access+parks+hydrography+osm_: Waterfront Public Access Areas (WPAA) · NYC Parks Properties · NYC Planimetric Database: Hydrography · OpenStreetMap pedestrian network (OSMnx walk graph)

Architecture.label: Weighted landmark proximity
Architecture.method: Sample the street centerline every 40 m. For LPC landmark lots within 300 m, apply Gaussian distance weights (σ = 100 m) and average all samples. Higher values indicate stronger exposure to recognized landmarks

Nature.label: Recorded trees
Nature.method: Count mapped tree points within 30 m of each street segment. Divide by segment length in kilometres, using a minimum length of 80 m to avoid inflated short-segment values. Higher values mean denser recorded tree presence

Nature.label: Park adjacency
Nature.method: Sample points along the street centerline and side offsets at 20 m and 40 m. Divide points inside official park polygons by all valid sample points. Higher values indicate stronger spatial adjacency to park land

Nature.label: Tree-canopy cover
Nature.method: Create a 20 m buffer on both sides of the street and intersect it with the 2021 land-cover raster. Divide canopy-class pixel area by total valid classified area × 100. Higher values indicate more overhead tree cover

Culture.label: Cultural POI proximity
Culture.method: Map museums, galleries, theatres, libraries, and similar cultural destinations. For locations within 450 m, sum Gaussian distance-decay weights (σ = 150 m) along the street. Higher values indicate stronger nearby cultural access

Quiet & Relax.label: Noise-complaint intensity
Quiet & Relax.method: Filter geolocated NYC 311 noise complaints to the latest 12 months. Sum Gaussian distance weights for reports within 150 m (σ = 50 m), then reverse the percentile. Fewer nearby complaints rank higher

Quiet & Relax.label: Roadway width
Quiet & Relax.method: Read roadway width in feet from NYC LION for each street segment. Convert values to Manhattan-relative percentiles and reverse them so narrower streets rank higher. This is a quietness proxy, not a measured sound level

Spatial Comfort.label: Mapped sidewalk coverage
Spatial Comfort.method: Sample roughly every 20 m along the street and add left/right offsets at 5, 8, 11, and 14 m. Divide points inside mapped sidewalk polygons by all valid points. Higher values indicate wider or more continuous sidewalk coverage

Spatial Comfort.label: Walking distance to seating
Spatial Comfort.method: Locate public seating points on the walkable network. From each street midpoint, calculate the shortest walking distance to the nearest seat, capped at 500 m. Shorter distances indicate easier access to rest

Spatial Comfort.label: Pedestrian-ramp coverage
Spatial Comfort.method: Identify evaluable pedestrian crossing nodes along the street. Check whether at least one recorded curb ramp lies within 20 m of each node, then divide covered nodes by all eligible nodes. Higher values mean more documented ramp provision

Urban Vibrancy.label: POI diversity × quantity
Urban Vibrancy.method: Collect OSM places within 150 m of the street midpoint and group them by activity type. Compute normalized Shannon diversity H and multiply it by ln(1 + POI count). Higher values indicate both more places and greater use diversity

Urban Vibrancy.label: Observed pedestrian flow
Urban Vibrancy.method: Standardize pedestrian-sensor observations by hour and period to make locations comparable. Use the median valid hourly pedestrian count and compare it with the POI-based vibrancy model. This is validation evidence, not a full-street score

Food & Retail.label: Food and retail proximity
Food & Retail.method: Extract mapped restaurants, cafés, bars, shops, and other retail POIs. At street samples, sum Gaussian proximity values for locations within 150 m (σ = 50 m). Higher values indicate stronger nearby food and retail availability

Scenic & Visual.label: Scenic POI proximity
Scenic & Visual.method: Select OSM viewpoints, public art, fountains, memorials, and monuments. Compute Gaussian distance weights within 300 m (σ = 100 m) along street samples. Higher values indicate greater proximity to scenic features

Scenic & Visual.label: Walking distance to waterfront
Scenic & Visual.method: Verify public waterfront entries and their links to walkable paths. Calculate the shortest pedestrian-network route from each street midpoint to the nearest valid entrance. Shorter distances indicate easier public access to waterfront views

Walkability.label: Connected junctions
Walkability.method: Construct the walkable-road topology from NYC LION segments. Identify junctions meeting at least three segments and count those within 250 m of each street midpoint. Higher counts indicate more route choices and connections

Walkability.label: Walking-network detour
Walkability.method: Sample feasible nearby origin–destination pairs around each street. Divide the shortest pedestrian-network distance by straight-line distance and take the median. Ratios closer to 1 indicate less detour and more direct walking

Access & Safety.label: Pedestrian-injury crash intensity
Access & Safety.method: Filter three years of reported collisions involving pedestrian injury or death. Sum Gaussian proximity weights for crash points within 120 m (σ = 40 m) and reverse the percentile. Fewer nearby crashes rank higher

Access & Safety.label: Crime-report proximity
Access & Safety.method: Combine NYPD historic and current-YTD complaint records, deduplicate incident IDs, and retain felony and misdemeanor cases. Sum Gaussian weights for reports within 300 m (σ = 100 m). Fewer reports rank higher, but this remains a proxy rather than personal risk

Environment.label: Distance to highways/ramps
Environment.method: Measure straight-line distance from each street midpoint to the nearest mapped highway or access ramp. Cap distances at 1,500 m and rank farther distances higher. This acts as a proximity-based environmental exposure proxy

Environment.label: Impervious surface cover
Environment.method: Buffer each street by 20 m on both sides and overlay the 2021 classified land-cover raster. Divide impervious-surface area by total valid raster area × 100. Lower values indicate less nearby hard-surface cover

Environment.label: Annual NO₂ area context
Environment.method: Read annual NO₂ concentration using the official DOHMH geography, period, and source units. Use this only as neighbourhood-scale environmental context; do not assign the value directly to individual street segments

Transit Connectivity.label: Entry-permitted subway entrances
Transit Connectivity.method: Keep only MTA entrances that allow passengers to enter. Count qualifying entrances within 400 m of each street midpoint. Higher values indicate more nearby access points, not higher service frequency

Transit Connectivity.label: Distance to subway entrance
Transit Connectivity.method: From each street midpoint, find the nearest MTA entrance that permits boarding access. Measure distance, cap it at 1,500 m, and reverse the Manhattan percentile. Shorter distances indicate stronger subway proximity
